Everything you need to run, integrate and inspect Mandate Wallet.

A complete first purchase

Connect your agent and buy an ETH statistics response

This tutorial follows one goal: use Codex CLI, Claude Code or Claude Desktop to buy an approved ETH statistics response and write a brief with its actual cost and evidence limits. You approve the scope in Rabby; the agent executes through MCP.

The local case starts with 1.00 mock USDC, a 0.15-USDC task budget and a 0.10-USDC per-payment cap. The task instruction allows one ETH purchase for at most 0.01 USDC. Leave BTC unpurchased to inspect the final revocation. Data is a fixed fixture, not live market information.

1Prepare software2Approve in Rabby3Connect MCP4Buy and recover5Review and revoke
Use Codex CLIUse Claude CodeUse Claude Desktop (GUI)First prepare the workspace

Use one host. CLI setup is in steps 08 or 09. The Claude Desktop graphical route is in 09.1–09.6 and includes the read-only check, then continues at step 11. Start at step 01 if the Gateway or owner permission is not ready. Installing MCP does not create an account or grant funds.

Recommended: use the setup wizard to deploy a local practice wallet and generate your agent connection. After the read-only check, continue at step 11. The detailed steps below preserve the manual workflow.

Open the setup wizard

The source component must be running. Testnet deployment requires external wallet signatures; installing an extension and enabling tools remain subject to the agent application’s approval.

STEP 01

Prepare software and files

The agent will buy one ETH statistics response and write a brief with its cost and evidence limits. Codex CLI, Claude Code or Claude Desktop runs the task; Rabby approves permissions; the workspace shows the records.

What to do

Choose one host: Codex CLI (08), Claude Code (09) or Claude Desktop Chat (09.1–09.6). The graphical route does not use the CLI setup. Use a desktop browser with Rabby for owner approval. The operator prepares the full checkout and builds the environment with the commands below.

Codex CLIClaude CodeClaude DesktopRabby
python3 scripts/bootstrap-sdk.py
CI=true pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
MANDATE_BUILD_REPORT_DIR=artifacts/sdk-build pnpm sdk:build

Before continuing

Have a running Gateway, the correct owner wallet and operator-provided connection instructions before continuing.

Continue: Connect the workspace

STEP 02

Connect the workspace

Connect the browser to the Gateway that owns the task configuration and durable order records. Opening the landing page does not select an account for the agent.

What to do

Obtain the Gateway URL, connection credential and network from the operator. For this local exercise use chain 31337, a 1.00 mock-USDC balance and a 0.01 mock-USDC controlled service. Choose Connect your own Gateway and enter those connection details. Do not enter a seed phrase.

Before continuing

Confirm the intended network, account and task. Keep the Gateway and its original database running.

Continue: Connect the Rabby owner wallet

STEP 03

Connect the Rabby owner wallet

Identify the account that can approve purchasing permissions. The owner wallet approves scope; a separate session signer executes within it.

What to do

Open the workspace in a desktop browser with Rabby, select Connect owner wallet, verify the site and choose the owner address displayed by the workspace. Select the configured chain and the operator-provided RPC. Use public test accounts only for the local exercise.

Before continuing

The owner and network must match. Connecting a wallet does not approve a permission transaction.

Continue: Create the ETH briefing task

STEP 04

Create the ETH briefing task

Convert the research goal into an explicit task with a spend limit and expiry. The budget is a maximum authorization, not the service price.

What to do

Create a task for an ETH statistics brief. Set total budget to 0.15 USDC, per-payment cap to 0.10 USDC and task duration to 60 minutes. The configured template includes ETH and BTC; buy ETH only and leave BTC unpurchased for the final revocation check. Select Review and confirm.

Before continuing

A review draft should appear. No permission is active until the owner transaction is confirmed.

Continue: Approve the task policy

STEP 05

Approve the task policy

The owner approves the task scope and limits. It becomes active only after the matching transaction is confirmed onchain.

What to do

Review the chain, account, owner, asset, limits, expiry, service resources and recipients. Continue to Rabby and compare from, to, value and calldata before signing. If the result is uncertain, reconcile the same request instead of creating another one.

Before continuing

The policy request must be confirmed and applied. A separate session grant is still required.

Continue: Approve a finite agent session

STEP 06

Approve a finite agent session

A policy defines allowed work; the session selects the signer and narrows the amount and duration available to that agent.

What to do

Select the newly created task and grant a 0.15-USDC session with a 0.10-USDC per-payment cap for 15 minutes, within the policy expiry. Review its task ID, session ID, signer and steps, then confirm in Rabby.

Before continuing

The session must be active. Record its actual IDs for the MCP profile; do not copy screenshot IDs.

Continue: Bind the agent profile to the approved task

STEP 07

Bind the agent profile to the approved task

Web task selection does not update the MCP server. The server is fixed to the task and session in its startup profile.

What to do

Ask the operator to export the selected task with the read-only command below. Save case-agent.json beside the original profile and set mandateId, sessionId and startBlock from the verified snapshot. Preserve key paths, the original databases, services and credential hash. A configured controller needs its separate approval workflow. Restart MCP after changing the profile.

pnpm sdk:cli context \
  --config PRIVATE_GATEWAY.json \
  --credential-file PRIVATE_CONNECTION.json \
  --task TASK_ID --output CURRENT_TASK.json

Before continuing

Have the absolute profile path and verify its task, session, signer and shared order store before connecting a host.

Continue with CodexContinue with Claude CodeContinue with Claude Desktop

STEP 08

Connect Mandate in Codex CLI

MCP exposes the purchasing tools to Codex without handing it the owner wallet key or replacing onchain approval.

What to do

Add the example to the trusted project’s .codex/config.toml and replace all absolute paths. The operator supplies MANDATE_CONNECTION_TOKEN in the launch environment; keep its value out of shared configuration. Start codex from that environment, inspect codex mcp list, and restart an existing session when needed. A desktop session must separately prove it inherited the credential and can call the tools. Run the included launch-host.mjs from the trusted project directory with the existing mode-0600 connection file. It forwards the credential without printing it; it does not install configuration or create permission.

[mcp_servers.mandate]
command = "/absolute/path/node"
args = ["/absolute/repository/dist/mandate-mcp.js",
        "--config", "/absolute/private/case-agent.json"]
cwd = "/absolute/repository"
env_vars = ["MANDATE_CONNECTION_TOKEN"]
startup_timeout_sec = 60
tool_timeout_sec = 120
default_tools_approval_mode = "writes"

Run from the trusted project directory

node /absolute/repository/docs/manual/launch-host.mjs codex \
  /absolute/private/PRIVATE_CONNECTION.json

Before continuing

Codex users continue to step 10. Claude Code users skip this configuration and use step 09. Listing a server alone does not prove tool access.

Follow the stated host and authorization boundaries; see the manual for source and verification details.

Continue to the read-only connection check

STEP 09

Use Claude Code instead

Claude Code is an alternative MCP host. Choose this route or Codex; do not run both purchases for the same exercise.

What to do

Merge the mandate entry into the project .mcp.json. Use actual absolute paths and reference MANDATE_CONNECTION_TOKEN from the launch environment. Start claude, inspect /mcp and review the project-server prompt. alwaysLoad makes these tools available; deferred discovery still requires loading the definitions. Run the included launch-host.mjs from the trusted project directory with the existing mode-0600 connection file. It forwards the credential without printing it; it does not install configuration or create permission.

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mandate": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "/absolute/path/node",
      "args": ["/absolute/repository/dist/mandate-mcp.js",
               "--config", "/absolute/private/case-agent.json"],
      "alwaysLoad": true,
      "env": {
        "MANDATE_CONNECTION_TOKEN": "${MANDATE_CONNECTION_TOKEN}"
      }
    }
  }
}

Run from the trusted project directory

node /absolute/repository/docs/manual/launch-host.mjs claude \
  /absolute/private/PRIVATE_CONNECTION.json

Before continuing

Continue to step 10 after the tools are callable. Codex users skip this step. Host approval is separate from the owner’s chain grant.

Follow the stated host and authorization boundaries; see the manual for source and verification details.

Continue to the read-only connection check

STEP 09.1

Open Claude Desktop extension settings

Use the local extension route in Claude Desktop Chat, separately from Claude Code and remote web connectors.

What to do

Open Claude → Settings → This computer → Extensions → Advanced settings. Prepare the MCPB, fixed Agent profile and matching private connection file from step 07. This macOS test extension requires Node 24.2–24.x.

Before continuing

Find Install extension. Follow organization policy if custom extensions are disabled.

Continue: Select the Mandate MCPB file

STEP 09.2

Select the Mandate MCPB file

Import the packaged local server without editing JSON or terminal environment variables.

What to do

Click Install extension and choose mandate-wallet-0.1.0.mcpb from output/desktop. Check its name, version, source and delivery hash before installing. Do not select the contract ZIP or manual source ZIP.

Native Claude Desktop screenshot. Actual installation and connection are tracked separately.

Continue: Review the extension capabilities

STEP 09.3

Review the extension capabilities

Review the local program and its eight tools before granting access.

What to do

Verify Mandate Wallet 0.1.0 by Mandate Labs and review the tools. mandate_get_context is read-only; mandate_call_service can spend test assets within the approved session. Owner approval remains in Rabby.

Bind the extension to the fixed task already checked in step 07.

Continue: Check the tools in the chat

STEP 09.5

Check the tools in the chat

Verify that the current conversation can use the installed extension.

What to do

Start a new Claude chat. Open + → Connectors and find Mandate Wallet. Inspect its eight tools. Review individual tool approvals when prompted; permanent auto-approval is not required. Restart Desktop if a newly configured server is missing.

Before continuing

Confirm tool availability, then make a read-only call.

Native Claude Desktop screenshot. Actual installation and connection are tracked separately.

Continue: Verify the account in a Claude chat

STEP 09.6

Verify the account in a Claude chat

Make one read-only call before using the same chat for the ETH brief case.

What to do

Send the prompt below and inspect the actual mandate_get_context result. Compare its network, wallet, task, session, budget and cash with the workspace. Approve only this call if prompted. Continue at step 11 for the purchase, recovery, brief and revocation.

Example instruction to send to your agent

Call only mandate_get_context and report chainId, wallet, mandateId, sessionId, session status, available budget and token cash. Do not quote, pay or modify permissions. Say explicitly if the tool cannot be called.

Before continuing

A matching real tool response proves connection. Plain claims or copied example values do not.

Native Claude Desktop screenshot. Actual installation and connection are tracked separately.

Continue: Give the agent a specific purchase task

STEP 10

Verify agent identity with a read-only call

Prove that the tools are callable and that the host is using the intended network, account, task and session before any purchase.

What to do

Send the read-only prompt below. Compare mandate_get_context with the workspace, including the IDs approved in step 06. Resolve missing tools, paths or launch credentials first. Stop if the profile still points to an older task.

Example instruction to send to your agent

Call only mandate_get_context and report chainId, wallet, mandateId, sessionId, session status, available budget and token cash. Do not quote, pay or modify permissions. Say explicitly if the tool cannot be called.

Before continuing

Report the 0.15-USDC authorization separately from the initial 1.00 mock-USDC balance. No purchase should occur in this step.

Continue: Give the agent a specific purchase task

STEP 11

Give the agent a specific purchase task

The task instruction narrows this exercise to one ETH purchase; the larger chain budget remains only a cap.

What to do

Ask the agent to buy the approved ETH response for at most 0.01 USDC and write a brief with the dataset, count, mean, actual cost, receipt and evidence limits. Leave BTC unpurchased. Use MCP for execution; do not also click the workspace run button.

Example instruction to send to your agent

Use Mandate to buy the approved ETH statistics response for at most 0.01 USDC and write a brief. Verify context and quote first. Do not buy BTC, raise limits, extend permission or change the recipient. Recover an already-paid failure with the same order. Report dataset, count, mean, cost, payment/delivery/result states, receipt hash and evidence limits.

Before continuing

The agent must stop if it needs a new service, recipient or larger permission. Test data must not be described as live market data.

Continue: Have the agent verify the quote

STEP 12

Have the agent verify the quote

A quote identifies the price, chain, asset and recipient without paying. Check it before executing the service.

What to do

The agent selects the ETH serviceId from context and calls mandate_quote_service. Verify 0.01 USDC and the approved recipient, chain and asset. Catalog discovery does not expand permission. The workspace image shows the corresponding service information, not a host tool-call screen.

Before continuing

Proceed only if the quote also satisfies the stricter 0.01-USDC instruction, even though the chain per-payment cap is 0.10 USDC.

Continue: Run the purchase and interpret the service error

STEP 13

Run the purchase and interpret the service error

The agent calls mandate_call_service within its approved session. Registration and budget reservation precede release of the payment signature.

What to do

The controlled local merchant deliberately returns HTTP 500 after its first payment. Interpret paid / failed / unchecked as a confirmed payment with delivery outstanding. Preserve the same order, nonce, settlement hash and database; an HTTP error is not evidence of nonpayment.

Before continuing

The 0.01-USDC payment remains recorded and occupied. Do not invent a data result or make a replacement purchase.

Continue: Recover delivery using the original paid order

STEP 14

Recover delivery using the original paid order

Resume delivery with the existing payment instead of buying the same data again.

What to do

Reconcile first if payment is uncertain; otherwise call mandate_call_service again with the original ETH serviceId and unchanged order store. Check mandate_get_task and mandate_get_receipt, then compare settlement hashes before and after recovery.

Example instruction to send to your agent

Recover the existing paid ETH order using the same serviceId, order, nonce and database. Reconcile first; compare settlement hashes and confirm the total payment did not increase.

Before continuing

Expect paid / returned / valid, the same settlement hash and a total cost of 0.01 USDC. Screenshot hashes are historical examples, not new run results.

Continue: Write the brief from the validated result

STEP 15

Write the brief from the validated result

Use the purchased result to finish the task, with enough cost and receipt information for another reader to check it.

What to do

Use validatedResultSummary. The fixed ETH fixture has three observations and mean 110; it is not a current ETH price. If the live tool response lacks the summary, report that gap instead of copying the example. Include the actual 0.01-USDC payment, three outcome states and current receipt hash.

Historical Codex result (2026-10-14)
validatedResultSummary:
  datasetId: mandate-fixed-fixture-v2
  asset: ETH
  count: 3
  mean: 110
paymentState: paid
serviceState: returned
resultState: valid
value: 10000  (0.01 USDC)

Before continuing

Produce a complete brief, then verify it against the same task in the workspace. The historical Codex excerpt below is an example format, not a newly executed purchase.

Continue: Reconcile the brief with workspace payment records

STEP 16

Reconcile the brief with workspace payment records

Match the agent’s narrative to durable order and chain records instead of treating model prose as payment evidence.

What to do

Select the same task and compare service ID, registration, settlement and outcome states with the agent receipt. In this isolated example, one 0.01-USDC purchase changes the initial balance from 1.00 to 0.99; occupied is 0.01 and unused authorization is 0.14. Gas is separate.

Before continuing

The records must agree, recovery must not add a payment, and BTC must still be unpurchased. Expired unused authorization cannot be spent.

Continue: Export evidence for review

STEP 17

Export evidence for review

Preserve verification material that can be checked separately from the agent’s brief. A redacted MCP receipt is not a complete evidence bundle.

What to do

Select the ETH step on Evidence. Keep bodies hidden by default, or disclose only within the administrator-approved public-data policy. Export the JSON and run independent checks with the separately trusted verification profile.

Before continuing

Save the evidence and report, with no connection credential or production RPC key in the shared material.

Continue: Interpret what the report proves

STEP 18

Interpret what the report proves

Separate verified financial and record facts from missing HTTPS-origin or complete-history guarantees.

What to do

Inspect registration-and-authority, budget and payment. Body disclosure affects request/result checks. Even when result is confirmed, https-source or history-completeness can remain incomplete. A separate process under the same OS administrator does not prove hostile-host isolation.

Before continuing

Keep those limits in the final brief. Do not describe an overall incomplete report as fully verified.

Continue: Revoke the session when the task is complete

STEP 19

Revoke the session when the task is complete

Stop future payments from the session. Closing the agent or deleting its MCP entry does not revoke onchain authority.

What to do

Select Revoke session for the current task, or let mandate_request_revoke prepare the unsigned request for owner review. Confirm the exact revocation in Rabby and wait for chain reconciliation. The wallet image is a dated historical reference.

Before continuing

The session must be revoked while existing payments and order records remain intact. Revocation does not refund the service.

Continue: Verify revocation and finish the case

STEP 20

Verify revocation and finish the case

Check that the owner stopped future purchasing while preserving the delivered result and historical records.

What to do

Call mandate_get_context again and distinguish revoked from expired. Inspect the unpurchased BTC step; do not submit another payment merely to demonstrate rejection. Existing paid-order reads or delivery recovery are not new payments. Save the brief, receipt and evidence before disconnecting.

Before continuing

The finished case has an MCP-produced ETH brief, one 0.01-USDC payment, reconcilable records and a terminated session.

Recorded reference images come from separate local and wallet runs. Configuration blocks are instructions, not screenshots of a newly connected host. Historical host acceptance records are retained in artifacts/m4/host-acceptance.json. Claude Desktop setup screenshots document only the recorded screens; the package has independent MCP tests. Installation and model-driven tool calls are tracked separately. This update submits no live purchase or permission transaction.

New to Mandate? Watch the complete interactive flow without a wallet.

What Mandate provides

Mandate Wallet gives an agent finite purchasing authority. The owner defines the asset, recipient, task steps, budget, per-payment cap and expiry. A local Gateway, MCP server, CLI and Web workspace share the same purchase client and persistent order history.

ComponentResponsibility
Owner walletReviews and signs permissions; the Gateway does not hold this owner key.
Agent + MCPRequests approved services through a fixed tool surface. Tool access does not create spending authority.
Gateway + operatorChecks scope, registers the commitment, keeps the original nonce and reconciles uncertain results.
Immutable accountEnforces policy/session budgets and verifies the registered EIP-3009 authorization with ERC-1271.
Merchant / facilitatorReturns payment terms, settles the approved authorization and provides service or receipt claims.
Independent verifierChecks disclosed evidence against separately trusted deployment identity and retained checkpoints.

Run from source

The full SDK is installed from this project checkout, not a published npm package. Requirements: Node 24.x (>=24.2), pnpm 11.25.0, Python 3.12+ and Foundry 1.5.1. Bootstrap fetches pinned dependency sources and checks their hashes.

python3 scripts/bootstrap-sdk.py
CI=true pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
MANDATE_BUILD_REPORT_DIR=artifacts/sdk-build pnpm sdk:build
pnpm sdk:demo artifacts/sdk-demo

The demo runs real local EVM and HTTP processes with a mintable test token. It buys one approved data step, recovers the same paid order after HTTP 500, exports evidence, runs independent checks and revokes the finite session. It does not use public funds.

Inspect summary.json, first-agent.json, recovered.json, evidence-bundle.json and verification.json in the output folder. An incomplete verification report can still pass financial/record checks while explicitly lacking HTTPS-origin or complete-history guarantees.

Use the Owner workspace

New users can start with the interactive walkthrough for the task, limited approval, purchase, same-order recovery and revocation. The walkthrough only updates its page illustration; it connects no wallet and submits no transaction.

The preset local test task uses a public test account without an owner signer in the browser. Connecting a personal wallet cannot renew its expired permission. The workspace explains this and offers the walkthrough or connection to your own Gateway. Guidance in your own workspace targets a concrete policy-renewal or session-grant control.

Open the App on the computer running the trusted Gateway. The local demo button uses only the public mock fixture. A real Gateway requires its own connection credential; it is not a seed phrase or private key and is held in browser memory only.

pnpm m6:serve --config PRIVATE_GATEWAY.json \
  --credential-file PRIVATE_CONNECTION.json

Choose or create a task, review the owner transaction, confirm it in your external wallet, then grant a separate finite session. Quote an approved service before running its step. The guide locates a control; it never confirms a wallet request or executes a business action for you.

Changing the display language does not reconnect the wallet, reissue a quote, change a transaction or clear an open form. Task descriptions, addresses, identifiers, raw calldata and exported JSON are not translated.

Connect an agent through MCP

Claude Desktop Chat supports the graphical MCPB import route with the fixed Agent profile and connection file. View graphical setup and screenshots

Build the local stdio server, point your MCP host at the absolute dist/mandate-mcp.js path, pass --config with the administrator-approved agent profile and inherit MANDATE_CONNECTION_TOKEN from the trusted environment. Do not put an owner key or literal credential into a shared host configuration.

pnpm m4:build
node /absolute/repository/dist/mandate-mcp.js \
  --config /absolute/private/agent-a.json
ToolBehavior
mandate_get_contextRead identity, policy, grant and cash.
mandate_request_authorizationPrepare an unsigned policy replacement; does not sign or activate authority.
mandate_search_servicesDiscover untrusted directory metadata.
mandate_quote_serviceRead approved service terms without paying.
mandate_call_serviceRun or resume one approved step with its original order.
mandate_get_taskRead payment, delivery and result independently.
mandate_get_receiptExport a redacted receipt.
mandate_request_revokePrepare unsigned session revocation; chain confirmation is required.

Use separate sessions and credentials per agent while sharing the configured store for a shared task budget. The supported hosts have separate installation instructions in mandate/gateway/README.zh-CN.md. A connected MCP server does not mean the model has loaded every deferred tool or that the owner has granted funds.

SDK and CLI

Use the Node entry mandate/sdk/index.ts or the browser entry mandate/sdk/browser.ts. Never bundle the Node entry or private runtime into a browser. Purchases and recovery use the same task/service identity and persistent store.

import { loadGateway, MandateWorkspace } from './mandate/sdk/index.js';
const runtime = await loadGateway(configPath, connectionToken);
try {
  const workspace = await MandateWorkspace.create(runtime.tools, verificationProfile);
  await workspace.quote(taskId, serviceId);
  const order = await workspace.call(taskId, serviceId);
  const state = await workspace.snapshot(taskId);
  const bundle = await workspace.evidence(taskId, serviceId);
} finally { runtime.close(); }
pnpm sdk:cli context --config PRIVATE_GATEWAY.json --credential-file CONNECTION.json
pnpm sdk:cli quote --config PRIVATE_GATEWAY.json --credential-file CONNECTION.json --service SERVICE_ID
pnpm sdk:cli call --config PRIVATE_GATEWAY.json --credential-file CONNECTION.json --service SERVICE_ID
pnpm sdk:cli reconcile --config PRIVATE_GATEWAY.json --credential-file CONNECTION.json

Owner-create and owner-action return unsigned review requests. Owner-broadcast records the original transaction hash; owner-reconcile checks its canonical effect. They do not load an owner key. The detailed profile and disclosure schemas are in the SDK quick start.

Authorization and budget semantics

USDC amounts use six decimal places: 0.15 USDC = 150000 atomic units, and 0.10 USDC = 100000. Budget is a limit, not wallet cash. The shared root and each finite session must both allow a payment. Gas is separate from the procurement budget.

OperationEffect
Create mandateCreates root scope; does not automatically grant an agent session.
Grant sessionApproves one signer, explicit steps, a finite budget, cap and expiry within the root.
Replace / pauseChanges the policy version; previous grants become stale. Unpause alone does not restore scope.
RevokeIrreversible for the revoked object. Existing paid or unresolved commitments stay occupied.
Release expiredOnly an expired unused authorization nonce is eligible. A paid nonce is not refundable by this function.

Payment and recovery

The current path is x402 v2 exact with EIP-3009 and a deployed immutable ERC-1271 account. The session signs the registration context and exact payment parameters. Registration and budget reservation succeed before the payment signature is sent. ERC-1271 checks the latest mandate/session state at settlement.

Observed stateNext action
Registered / pending / unknownReconcile the same step. Keep the original nonce and occupied budget; do not issue a replacement order.
Paid + service failedRecover delivery using the original paid order, even after permission expires or is revoked.
Paid + invalid resultInspect evidence. Do not buy the same step again.
Consumed / canceled without confirmed paymentInspect original chain evidence and occupancy. Do not replace the nonce.

Merchant/facilitator compatibility is specific to a network, asset and signature wrapper. The tested controlled facilitator supports this path; this is not a claim that every Bazaar merchant or third-party facilitator accepts smart-account/session signatures. Permit2 and ERC-7710 are not implemented in this payment path.

Contracts and interfaces

MandateFactory uses CREATE2 with an owner/asset/user-salt namespace. A caller can create an account only for itself; creating an existing address returns it. MandateAccount is not upgradeable. Its EIP-712 domain is MandateWallet version 2; the asset must expose EIP-3009 state and a six-decimal domain.

Canonical ABI signatureBehavior
createMandate(bytes32,bytes32,(uint256,uint256,uint64),(bytes32,address,address)[],(bytes32,bytes32,bytes32)[])Owner: create root policy and approved merchants/steps.
grantSession(bytes32,bytes32,address,uint256,uint256,uint64,bytes32[])Owner: approve one finite signer/session subset.
isValidSignature(bytes32,bytes)ERC-1271: verify the registered live EIP-3009 authorization.
ownerWithdraw(address,uint256)Owner: transfer account tokens; does not reduce recorded budget occupancy.
registerPayment((bytes32,uint64,bytes32,uint64,bytes32,bytes32,bytes32,bytes32,address,uint256,uint256,uint256,bytes32),bytes,bytes)Session proof + approved quote: reserve payment and budget.
releaseExpired(bytes32)Release expired unused authorization occupancy.
replacePolicy(bytes32,(uint256,uint256,uint64),(bytes32,address,address)[],(bytes32,bytes32,bytes32)[])Owner: replace limits/scope while retaining occupied funds.
revokeMandate(bytes32)Owner: irreversibly revoke the root.
revokeSession(bytes32,bytes32)Owner: irreversibly revoke one session.
setPaused(bytes32,bool)Owner: pause/unpause with a version change.

The account binds the deployment chain, owner, approved asset, policy version, session epoch, step, merchant, request/quote hashes, recipient, value, nonce and validity window. MAX_PAYMENT_SECONDS is 300; maximum configured merchants/steps are 32/64. Read-only getters expose policies, sessions, steps, merchants and commitments.

Open-source contracts

Download the MIT-licensed contract distribution below. It includes original Solidity sources, Foundry tests/configuration, the dependency import closure and its licenses, generated ABIs, historical verification inputs and a SHA-256 file manifest. It excludes Gateway profiles, keys, private runtime state and competition registration/proposal materials.

Download contracts (MIT)Release manifest
unzip mandate-contracts-v2.zip
cd mandate-contracts-v2
forge build --root mandate/contracts
forge test --root mandate/contracts

The original compiler settings are Solidity 0.8.26, optimizer enabled with 200 runs, viaIR and Cancun EVM. TestUSDC and MockUSDC are test fixtures, not production currency. The ZIP can be built without a private project profile. The complete source and reproduction guide are available in the public repository.

Evidence and disclosure

Payment, service delivery and result validation are independent outcomes. Onchain events prove recorded financial effects. An approved merchant signature proves a claim by that key. A local session attestation or salted Merkle proof proves the relevant retained commitment/disclosure, not the HTTPS origin or every unobserved action.

pnpm sdk:cli evidence --config PRIVATE_GATEWAY.json --credential-file CONNECTION.json \
  --verification-file VERIFY_PROFILE.json --service SERVICE_ID --output BUNDLE.json
pnpm sdk:cli verify --config PRIVATE_GATEWAY.json --credential-file CONNECTION.json \
  --verification-file VERIFY_PROFILE.json --service SERVICE_ID --output CHECKS.json

The verification profile independently pins chainId, wallet, asset, owner, walletRuntimeHash, RPCs and allowed disclosure. Do not derive those trust anchors from the untrusted bundle. Request/result disclosure is disabled by default; the UI can only narrow, never expand, the administrator-approved disclosure policy.

Common recovery cases

CaseResolution
Gateway unavailableStart the trusted loopback server, check its address and browser local-network permission, then reconnect. Never paste a wallet seed into the credential field.
Expired / paused / stale sessionThe owner must review the current policy and approve a finite current grant. Connecting a wallet alone does not restore authority.
Cash below quoteBudget increases do not add cash. The owner must fund the approved asset on the correct network.
RPC timeout / reorgKeep the original order/hash and reconcile canonical evidence before any new signature.
Merchant proof or terms mismatchStop and review configured signer, resource, recipient, asset and scheme. Directory metadata does not authorize a bypass.

Security and current limits

The owner can withdraw token cash even while commitments retain budget occupancy. Budgets are authorization limits, not escrow guarantees; an owner withdrawal can leave insufficient cash for later settlement.

The current system is a testnet engineering build, not an audited mainnet release. Owner and session/operator roles are separate, but processes controlled by one OS administrator do not provide hostile-host isolation. Independently controlled owner signing and separately managed evidence retention are needed for that boundary.

The account enforces financial scope and request/quote hashes, not the full off-chain session root. Controller checks rely on independent retained checkpoints and cannot prove activity they never observed. Bazaar text is untrusted. Mainnet writes, arbitrary execution, automatic swaps, Permit2 and ERC-7710 are outside this path.
